#Standardize data
#Z-scores
```{r hellinger, include=FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(vegan)

# Ensure data.table
setDT(pca_df)

# Identify numeric columns
numeric_cols <- sapply(pca_df, is.numeric)
numeric_colnames <- names(numeric_cols[numeric_cols])

# Exclude environmental / metadata columns
exclude_cols <- c(
  "sample_net_mesh",
  "Salinity_Min", "Salinity_Max", "Salinity_Avg",
  "Water_Temp_Min", "Water_Temp_Max", "Water_Temp_Avg",
  "Secchi.depth",
  "STD",
  "avg_chl_a",
  "Month",
  "Season", 
  "Date"
)

# Community columns only
community_cols <- setdiff(numeric_colnames, exclude_cols)

# Subset community matrix
community_df <- pca_df[, ..community_cols]

# Hellinger transform
community_hellinger <- decostand(
  as.matrix(community_df),
  method = "hellinger"
)

# Check for negative values
any(community_df < 0, na.rm = TRUE)

# Check for NAs
anyNA(community_df)
community_hellinger <- decostand(community_df, method = "hellinger")
print(community_hellinger)

community_hellinger <- as.data.table(community_hellinger)
setnames(community_hellinger, community_cols)

community_hellinger <- cbind(
  pca_df[, ..exclude_cols],
  community_hellinger
)
print(community_hellinger)
```
```{r pca plots NEW, include=FALSE}
# ===============================
# PCA with Hellinger community data + environmental vectors
# ===============================

library(data.table)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)

# Ensure data.table
setDT(community_hellinger)

# -------------------------------
# 1. Split data into roles
# -------------------------------

# Environmental variables (for envfit vectors)
env_df <- as.data.frame(
  community_hellinger[, ..exclude_cols] #looks good
)

# Community matrix (for PCA)
comm_mat <- as.matrix(
  community_hellinger[, ..community_cols]
) #looks good

# -------------------------------
# 2. Run PCA (NO scaling after Hellinger)
# -------------------------------

pca <- prcomp(comm_mat, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)

# -------------------------------
# 3. PCA scores for plotting
# -------------------------------

scores_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x)
scores_df <- cbind(scores_df, env_df)

# Base PCA plot
pca_plot <- ggplot(scores_df, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2,1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2,2], 1), "%)")
  )

# -------------------------------
# 4. Fit environmental vectors
# -------------------------------

envfit_res <- envfit(pca, env_df, permutations = 999)

vectors <- scores(envfit_res, display = "vectors")

# -------------------------------
# 5. Prepare vectors for plotting
# -------------------------------

arrow_scale <- 1  # adjust visually

vectors_df <- as.data.frame(vectors * arrow_scale)
vectors_df$env_var <- rownames(vectors_df)

# -------------------------------
# 6. Add vectors to PCA plot
# -------------------------------

pca_plot_new <- pca_plot +
  geom_segment(
    data = vectors_df,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = vectors_df,
    aes(x = PC1 * 1.1, y = PC2 * 1.1, label = env_var),
    color = "blue",
    size = 4
  )

print(pca_plot_new)

# -------------------------------
# 7. Save and open plot
# -------------------------------

ggsave("pca_plot_new.png", plot = pca_plot_new, dpi = 300)
browseURL("pca_plot_new.png")

```
```{r pca plots OLD, include=FALSE}
library(vegan)
library(ggfortify)
library(FactoMineR)
library(vcd)
library(factoextra)
library(data.table)

pca_df <- pca_df %>%
  mutate(
    Month = month(Date),
    Season = case_when(
      Month %in% 1:3 ~ "Winter",
      Month %in% 4:6 ~ "Spring",
      Month %in% 7:9 ~ "Summer",
      Month %in% 10:12 ~ "Fall"
    )
  )


#how copes fall out by env factor
# Replace 'data' with your data frame and adjust the column indices accordingly
# Replace '1:4' with the indices of the fixed environmental factors you want to include
pca_plot_1 <- fviz_pca_biplot(community_hellinger,

                         geom.ind = "point",

                         habillage = pca_df[,2],  # Include environmental factors

                         choose.vars = list(contrib = 2),

                         title = "PCA Plot 1"

)
print(pca_plot_1)

#how samples fall out by env factor
pca_plot_2 <- fviz_pca_ind(community_hellinger,

                            geom.ind = "point",

                            habillage = pca_df$Season,  # Include environmental factors

                            addEllipses = TRUE, ellipse.level = 0.95,

                            title = "PCA Plot Ram"

)
# Customize the plot as needed
print(pca_plot_2)

library(vegan)
library(factoextra)

# Suppose your environmental variables are columns in pca_df like this:
env_vars <- community_hellinger[, c("Water_Temp_Avg", "Salinity_Avg", "Secchi.depth", "avg_chl_a")]  # Replace with your numeric env variable names

pca_scores <- as.data.frame(community_hellinger$x)
#pca_scores$Season <- pca_df$Season

ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Season, shape = Season)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, stroke = 1.1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Winter" = 15, "Spring" = 16, "Summer" = 17, "Fall" = 18)) +

# Fit env vectors onto PCA result

pca_plot_3 <- fviz_pca_ind(
  community_hellinger,

) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Winter" = 15, "Spring" = 16, "Summer" = 17, "Fall" = 18)) +
  theme_minimal()

# Scale vectors for plotting (adjust the multiplier to get suitable arrow lengths)
arrow_scale <- 1  # tweak this to fit your plot

# Create a data frame of vectors
vectors_df <- as.data.frame(vectors * arrow_scale)
vectors_df$env_var <- rownames(vectors_df)

# Add arrows and labels to the plot
pca_plot_4 <- pca_4 +
  geom_segment(data = vectors_df,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")),
               color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_text(data = vectors_df,
            aes(x = PC1 * 1.1, y = PC2 * 1.1, label = env_var),
            color = "blue",
            size = 4)
print(pca_plot_4)
ggsave("pca_plot_4.png", plot = pca_plot_4, dpi = 300)
browseURL("pca_plot_4.png")

# Convert PCA scores to a data frame
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(community_hellinger$x)
pca_scores$Season <- pca_df$Season

# Calculate explained variance for axis labels
eig <- community_hellinger$sdev^2 / sum(community_hellinger$sdev^2)

# Create PCA plot
pca_4 <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Season, shape = Season)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, stroke = 1.1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Winter" = 15, "Spring" = 16, "Summer" = 17, "Fall" = 18)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(eig[1] * 100, 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(eig[2] * 100, 1), "%)"),
    title = "PCA Ram"
  ) +
  # Add horizontal and vertical lines at 0
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black")

print(pca_4)
ggsave("pca_plot_4.png", plot = pca_4, dpi = 300)
browseURL("pca_plot_4.png")

pca_plot_4 <- pca_4 +
  # Add arrows for environmental vectors
  geom_segment(
    data = vectors_df,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,  # prevent using Season etc.
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")),
    color = "blue", size = 0.75
  ) +
  
  # Add text labels for each vector
  geom_text(
    data = vectors_df,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(x = PC1 * 1.1, y = PC2 * 1.1, label = env_var),
    color = "blue", size = 3
  )

# Display it
print(pca_plot_4)

# Save it
ggsave("pca_plot_4_arrows.png", plot = pca_plot_4, dpi = 300)
browseURL("pca_plot_4_arrows.png")
```
